title: Radio Replay: Playing The Gender Card

sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: We begin today in Las Vegas, the year 2004.
sentences.zh: 今天我们从2004年的拉斯维加斯说起。

sentences.en: The scene, a high-stakes poker game.
sentences.zh: 场景是一场高额扑克游戏。

sentences.en: Our protagonist is a woman named Annie Duke.
sentences.zh: 我们的主角是一位名叫安妮·杜克的女性。

sentences.en: And with that top pair, Phil Hellmuth going all in with his 450,000 chips.
sentences.zh: 菲尔·赫尔穆特拿着顶对，押上了他所有的45万筹码。

sentences.en: put the pressure on Phil when she check-raised him.
sentences.zh: 在过牌加注后，给菲尔施加了压力。

sentences.en: This was the final hand of the World Series of

sentences.zh: 冠军锦标赛的最后一手牌。

sentences.en: They had these incredible Hall of Fame players, like Doyle Brunson,
sentences.zh: 当时在场的都是些传奇的入选名人堂的选手，比如多伊尔·布朗森，

sentences.en: who was a Hall of Famer, Johnny Chan, who was a Hall of Famer, and then Phil Hellmuth, who has the
sentences.zh: 他是名人堂成员，还有名人堂成员约翰尼·陈，以及菲尔·赫尔穆特，他拥有

sentences.en: most championships of anyone in the history of the World Series of Poker.
sentences.zh: 世界扑克系列赛历史上最多的冠军头衔。

sentences.en: Annie calls the all-in, and Phil sees what he's up againSt.
sentences.zh: 安妮跟注了全押，菲尔看到了他的对手是谁。

sentences.en: Annie and this guy, Phil, were the last two at the table.
sentences.zh: 安妮和这个叫菲尔的家伙，是桌上最后剩下的两人。

sentences.en: And Annie is overcome with emotion, seeing how close she is to winning this championship.
sentences.zh: 安妮情绪激动，因为她意识到自己离赢得冠军只有一步之遥。

sentences.en: Phil's standing up, pacing back and forth.
sentences.zh: 菲尔站了起来，来回踱步。

sentences.en: The dealer's laying out the cards
Annie has control of his hand.
Annie was the only woman in this competition.
sentences.zh: 安妮是这场比赛中唯一的女性。

sentences.en: She had knocked out eight guys, eight of the
sentences.zh: 她淘汰了八名选手，八名

sentences.en: best players in the world, to get to this point.
sentences.zh: 世界上最优秀的选手，才走到这一步。

sentences.en: Annie Duke is now one card away from $2 million.
sentences.zh: 安妮·杜克现在距离200万美元奖金只差一张牌。

sentences.en: But I didn't really feel like I deserved to be at that table.
sentences.zh: 但我当时真的觉得我不配坐在那张桌子上。

sentences.en: At that moment, Annie Duke was feeling the pressure of something that psychologists call
sentences.zh: 那一刻，安妮·杜克感受到了心理学家所说的

sentences.en: Let's say you think people have a certain stereotype about you.
sentences.zh: 假设你认为人们对你有某种刻板印象。

sentences.en: There's a part of you that's afraid that your actions and behavior will prove the stereotype
sentences.zh: 你内心深处会害怕自己的言行举止会证明这种刻板印象

sentences.en: I'm sort of thinking about, well, if I fold and I'm wrong, everybody's going to be like,
sentences.zh: 我当时就在想，如果我弃牌了但其实我错了，每个人都会说，

sentences.en: see, she plays like a girl.
sentences.zh: 看吧，她打牌就像个女人。

sentences.en: Like, look how he pushed her around.
sentences.zh: 就像是，看他怎么把她耍得团团转。

sentences.en: But Annie's story is also about a second idea, one that often has a positive outcome.
sentences.zh: 但安妮的故事也涉及第二个概念，一个往往会带来积极结果的概念。

sentences.en: This idea is called stereotype tax.
sentences.zh: 这个概念被称为“刻板印象红利”。

sentences.en: That's when a stereotype that others have about you
sentences.zh: 那是当别人对你的刻板印象

sentences.en: If somebody was at the table who was so emotionally invested in the fact that I was a woman,
sentences.zh: 如果桌上有人因为我是女性而对我投入了过多的情绪，

sentences.en: given that they're treating me that way, how can I come up with the best strategy to take their money?
sentences.zh: 既然他们这样对待我，我该如何制定最佳策略来赢走他们的钱呢？

sentences.en: Because I guess in the end, isn't that the best revenge?
sentences.zh: 因为我想，归根结底，这难道不是最好的报复吗？

sentences.en: Annie had started playing poker in 1994.
By the time she got to that championship game 10 years later,
sentences.zh: 到10年后她参加那场冠军赛时，

sentences.en: she had basically figured out how to make stereotypes about women in poker work for her.
sentences.zh: 她基本上已经摸索出如何利用扑克界对女性的刻板印象为自己服务了。

sentences.en: So I can tell you that the first year that I played in the World Series of Poker main event,
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，我参加世界扑克系列赛主赛事的第一年，

sentences.en: which was in 1994, 3% of the entrants were women.
sentences.zh: 也就是1994年，参赛者中只有3%是女性。

sentences.en: And last year, that number would have been the same.
sentences.zh: 而去年，这个数字依然差不多。

sentences.en: So this is an extraordinarily male-dominated sport.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一项极其男性主导的运动。

sentences.en: I was generally the only woman at the table.
sentences.zh: 我通常是桌上唯一的女性。

sentences.en: I had to really love that game in order to be willing to expose myself to a lot of the behavior
sentences.zh: 我必须真心热爱这个游戏，才愿意让自己去面对我所经历的

sentences.en: There were people who were incredibly welcoming.
There was one guy who I lost a pot to, and he said,
sentences.zh: 有一次我输给了一个家伙，他说，

sentences.en: don't cry, I'll give you your money back if we go across the street to the Northern.
sentences.zh: 别哭，如果我们去街对面的北方酒店，我会把钱还给你。

sentences.en: And the Northern was a hotel.
And I got called a lot of bad things.
sentences.zh: 我被骂过很多难听的话。

sentences.en: But to think about it as, okay, given that this person is viewing me in a way that I find disrespectful,
sentences.zh: 但如果换个角度想，既然这个人以一种我不觉得被尊重的方式看待我，

sentences.en: try to separate yourself from your emotional reaction to that and think about how you can use that to your advantage.
sentences.zh: 那就试着将自己从情绪反应中抽离出来，思考如何利用这一点来为自己谋利。

sentences.en: Annie had learned to make her opponents pay, literally pay, for the stereotypes they held about women.
sentences.zh: 安妮学会了让对手付出代价，字面意义上的代价，为他们对女性持有的刻板印象买单。

sentences.en: At the poker table, for example, I sort of in my head divided people into three categories.
sentences.zh: 在扑克桌上，我基本上在心里把人分成了三类。

sentences.en: One was the flirting chauvinist, and that person was really viewing me in a way that was sexual.
sentences.zh: 第一类是调情沙文主义者，那个人确实以一种带有性意味的方式看待我。

sentences.en: And not as blatantly as the guy who invited her back to the Great Northern Hotel.
sentences.zh: 而且不像那个邀请她去大北方酒店的家伙那么露骨。

sentences.en: These were just guys who sometimes seemed more concerned about getting Annie to like them than they were about winning.
sentences.zh: 这些人只是看起来比起赢牌，更关心如何让安妮喜欢他们。

sentences.en: Like they'd show me their whole cards when they were done with the hand to show me whether it was a good fold or not.
sentences.zh: 比如他们打完牌后会向我展示底牌，想让我看看他们弃牌弃得对不对。

sentences.en: They'd kind of tell me during the hand if I was alone with them in the hand, you know, what they had.
sentences.zh: 如果我和他们单独对局，他们会在牌局中告诉我他们拿了什么牌。

sentences.en: They were trying to make nice with you.
They were trying to make nice with me, exactly.
sentences.zh: 他们想和我套近乎，没错。

sentences.en: I never did go out on a date with any of them, but, you know, it was kind of flirtatious at the table,
sentences.zh: 我从来没和他们中的任何一个人约会过，但你知道，桌上确实有点调情的意味，

sentences.en: and I could use that to my advantage.
sentences.zh: 我可以利用这一点为我所用。

sentences.en: Then, there's a second kind of guy.
What I would call the disrespecting chauvinist, who mainly just thought that women weren't creative,
sentences.zh: 我会称之为不尊重人的沙文主义者，他们主要认为女性缺乏创造力，

sentences.en: that they could only think one level deep.
sentences.zh: 认为她们只能进行浅层思考。

sentences.en: So they didn't believe that you knew how to bluff, for example, because that's a level deep in your thinking.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不相信你知道如何诈唬，因为那需要更深一层的思考。

sentences.en: They didn't think that you really had creativity.
sentences.zh: 他们认为你根本没有创造力。

sentences.en: They thought you were very straightforward in the way that you play because, you know, you're a girl.
sentences.zh: 他们认为你的打法非常直白，因为，你知道，你是个女孩。

sentences.en: So they assume that you're naive, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上认为你很天真。

sentences.en: So there are strategies that you can use against them.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以利用一些策略来对付他们。

sentences.en: Mainly, you can bluff those people a lot.
sentences.zh: 主要是，你可以经常诈唬这些人。

sentences.en: And then there's a third kind of guy, perhaps the most reckless.
sentences.zh: 然后是第三种人，也许是最鲁莽的。

sentences.en: This is a guy who would do anything to avoid being beaten by a woman.
sentences.zh: 这种人为了避免输给女人，什么事都做得出来。

sentences.en: You couldn't bluff them because they would call you all the time for fear that you might be bluffing them.
sentences.zh: 你没法诈唬他们，因为他们总是会跟注，生怕你是在诈唬他们。

sentences.en: And then they would also try to push you around a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还会试图把你耍得团团转。

sentences.en: So they would play extremely aggressively against you.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会针对你打得极其激进。

sentences.en: They'd be trying to bluff you all the time because the best thing that could happen to them was that they bluffed you.
sentences.zh: 他们会一直试图诈唬你，因为对他们来说最好的结果就是成功诈唬了你。

sentences.en: And then they could show you that they had a terrible hand and like be like, ha ha, little girl, look what happened to you.
sentences.zh: 然后他们可以向你展示他们拿了一手烂牌，然后说，哈哈，小姑娘，看看你遭遇了什么。

sentences.en: Because that would confirm that everything that they believed about you was true.
sentences.zh: 因为那会证实他们关于你的一切偏见都是正确的。

sentences.en: So you can just sort of wait until they, what I say is, until they would impale themselves on your chips.
sentences.zh: 所以你只需要等着，用我的话说，等着他们撞在你的筹码上自取灭亡。

sentences.en: I have to ask you, though, so it's clear that thinking about this mathematically and in a very detached and unemotional way gave you an edge at the poker table.
sentences.zh: 但我必须问你，很明显，以数学的、非常客观且不带感情的方式思考，确实让你在扑克桌上占据了优势。

sentences.en: And I can clearly see how that's very smart.
sentences.zh: 我完全能看出这非常聪明。

sentences.en: At some level, you also are processing how people actually are behaving toward you.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你也在处理人们实际上是如何对待你的。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if you could talk a minute about how this felt.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能不能花点时间谈谈这种感觉。

sentences.en: Most of the time, I would sort of say, I have emotions about this.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，我会对自己说，我对这些有情绪。

sentences.en: I'm going to set them aside and deal with them later.
sentences.zh: 我要把它们放在一边，以后再处理。

sentences.en: And then I would leave the table and drive home in tears.
sentences.zh: 然后我会离开牌桌，开车回家时泪流满面。

sentences.en: In her first 10 years at the poker table, Annie was able to compartmentalize her emotions.
sentences.zh: 在打扑克的前十年里，安妮能够将自己的情绪隔离开来。

sentences.en: And she won a lot of money doing this, using stereotype tax to her advantage.
sentences.zh: 她靠这样做赢了很多钱，利用刻板印象红利为自己谋利。

sentences.en: That was until 2004 at the Tournament of Champions.
Intimidation is such a big part of being a successful player.
sentences.zh: 恐吓是成为一名成功选手的重要部分。

sentences.en: Is that going to come into play at this table, you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为这在这一桌上会发挥作用吗？

sentences.en: In fact, these players know each other so well, if one of them sneezes, somebody else has already handed them a handkerchief.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些选手彼此太熟悉了，如果其中一个人打喷嚏，另一个人早就递上手帕了。

sentences.en: Actually, at least for Annie, that wasn't true.
sentences.zh: 其实，至少对安妮来说，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: She had never played poker on TV before, and she was pretty sure she had been invited as the token woman, that she was way out of her league.
sentences.zh: 她以前从未在电视上打过扑克，她很确定自己是被邀请作为象征性的女性代表，她觉得自己的水平远不及其他人。

sentences.en: She thought that ESPN, televising the game in this way for the first time, just thought it was good optics to have her there.
sentences.zh: 她认为ESPN第一次以这种方式转播比赛，只是觉得有她在场画面效果更好。

sentences.en: And I had just gotten lucky, and now everybody was going to know it, and what they were saying was true.
sentences.zh: 我只是运气好，现在每个人都要知道了，他们说的都是真的。
你觉得自己是个冒牌货。

sentences.en: You were facing a very difficult situation here, which is you're not just juggling with what's happening at the poker table,
sentences.zh: 你当时面临着非常困难的处境，不仅要应付扑克桌上发生的事情，

sentences.en: but you're juggling with all this other psychological crap, in a way, that just makes it hard to focus on what it is that you're actually doing.
sentences.zh: 还要应付所有这些心理上的垃圾，这让你很难专注于你正在做的事情。

sentences.en: And in so many ways, that to me is a perfect illustration of stereotype threat.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这对我来说是“刻板印象威胁”的完美例证。

sentences.en: It shows that when there's a stereotype that's in the air, when there's a stereotype that multiple people believe, even if you don't believe it yourself,
sentences.zh: 它表明，当空气中弥漫着一种刻板印象，当多人相信这种刻板印象时，即使你自己并不相信，

sentences.en: if you're the person who is potentially at the receiving end of that stereotype,
sentences.zh: 如果你是那个可能成为刻板印象受害者的人，

sentences.en: it affects your behavior in such a way that you become more likely to make the stereotype come true.
sentences.zh: 它会以某种方式影响你的行为，使你更有可能让这种刻板印象成真。

sentences.en: I think that that's completely true.
It was always in the back of my mind, like, do they really respect me?
sentences.zh: 它总是萦绕在我的脑海里，比如，他们真的尊重我吗？

sentences.en: Why are they talking to me?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要和我说话？

sentences.en: Is it just because they are thinking about me in a different way, like they want to be friends with me because I'm a girl, or do they actually respect my play?
sentences.zh: 是因为他们以不同的方式看待我，比如因为我是女孩所以想和我交朋友，还是他们真的尊重我的牌技？

sentences.en: There was one hand, Annie says, when stereotype threat got the better of her.
sentences.zh: 安妮说，有一次牌局，刻板印象威胁战胜了她。

sentences.en: So in this particular hand where I had two tens.
sentences.zh: 在那手牌里，我有两张十。

sentences.en: Which is a pretty good hand.
sentences.zh: 这是一手相当不错的牌。

sentences.en: It was good enough that there wasn't a huge chance that her opponent, this guy, Greg Raymer, had a better hand.
sentences.zh: 好到她的对手，那个叫格雷格·雷默的家伙，拿到更好牌的几率并不大。

sentences.en: But there was still a chance.
As a professional poker player, this is the kind of hand that you evaluate in a matter of seconds.
sentences.zh: 作为一名职业扑克选手，这是那种你几秒钟内就能评估出来的牌。

sentences.en: So I really needed to eliminate that hand as a possibility, and I was having a lot of trouble doing that
sentences.zh: 所以我真的需要排除那种可能性，但我很难做到，

sentences.en: because I was so afraid of making this really bad big decision on television and having everyone say, I told you so.
sentences.zh: 因为我太害怕在电视上做出这个糟糕的重大决定，让每个人都说，我早就告诉过你了。

sentences.en: This was a pivotal hand, but a lot of the significance was really just in Annie's head.
sentences.zh: 这是一手关键牌，但很多意义其实只是在安妮的脑海里。

sentences.en: If she folded, but really had the best hand...
sentences.zh: 如果她弃牌了，但其实她拿的是最好的牌……

sentences.en: Everybody's going to be like, see, she plays like a girl.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会说，看吧，她打牌就像个女人。

sentences.en: Like, look how he pushed her around.
sentences.zh: 就像是，看他怎么把她耍得团团转。

sentences.en: And if I called and I was wrong, then I could come up with a whole other thing.
sentences.zh: 如果我跟注了但判断错了，那我还能再想出别的办法来。

sentences.en: Like, look how bad she is.
sentences.zh: 比如，看看她打得有多烂。

sentences.en: Didn't she know that he had the best hand?
sentences.zh: 她难道不知道他拿的是最好的牌吗？

sentences.en: Like, any idiot would have known that, you know.
sentences.zh: 任何白痴都该知道这一点，你懂的。

sentences.en: And that was running in my head as I was trying to make this decision.
sentences.zh: 我在做这个决定的时候，脑子里一直盘旋着这些想法。

sentences.en: So you're damned if you do, and you're damned if you don't.
sentences.zh: 所以你做也不是，不做也不是，左右为难。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until I kind of snapped to and saw this tell that he had.
sentences.zh: 直到我突然回过神来，注意到了他露出的一个马脚。

sentences.en: And when you say a tell, you mean what?
sentences.zh: 当你提到马脚时，你指的是什么？

sentences.en: So a tell is a physical...
sentences.zh: 马脚是指一种身体上的……

sentences.en: Well, it could be something verbal that somebody says that gives a clue.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也可能是某人说的话，透露出了一些线索。

sentences.en: But generally, when we talk about tells, we're talking about something physical that somebody does
sentences.zh: 但通常当我们谈论马脚时，指的是某人做出的某种身体动作，

sentences.en: that telegraphs the quality of their hand, or at least what they think the quality of their hand is.
sentences.zh: 这暴露了他们手牌的质量，或者至少是他们认为自己手牌的质量。

sentences.en: So Greg Raymer did something, which I haven't actually said what he actually did,
sentences.zh: 所以格雷格·雷默做了一些动作，我其实还没说他到底做了什么，

sentences.en: because I think that's unfair to him.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得这对他不公平。

sentences.en: But he did something that gave away the fact that his hand was very, very strong,
sentences.zh: 但他确实做了一些动作，泄露了他手牌非常、非常强的事实，

sentences.en: which allowed me to then fold.
sentences.zh: 这让我随后选择了弃牌。

sentences.en: And at that moment, I was actually quite confident in it.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，我其实对此相当自信。

sentences.en: But Annie's confidence in her decision was short-lived.
sentences.zh: 但安妮对她决定的自信并没有持续太久。

sentences.en: Another player came up to her during a break in the game.
sentences.zh: 比赛间隙，另一位选手走到她身边。

sentences.en: What he said kicked the stereotype threat in Annie's head into overdrive.
sentences.zh: 他说的话让安妮脑海中的“刻板印象威胁”瞬间加剧了。

sentences.en: Phil Hellmuth, right after that hand occurred, came up and just told me, like, what an idiot I was,
sentences.zh: 菲尔·赫尔穆特在那手牌结束后立刻走过来，直接说我有多蠢，

sentences.en: because clearly Greg Raymer had ace-king.
sentences.zh: 因为很明显格雷格·雷默拿的是A-K。

sentences.en: And I thought, oh my gosh, this is a guy who's like, now I think he's a 12-time world champion.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，天哪，这可是个——我现在认为他是12届世界冠军的人。

sentences.en: But at the time, he probably had, you know, seven world championships or something.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，他可能拿了七届世界冠军什么的。

sentences.en: And he seemed pretty confident that he had ace-king.
sentences.zh: 而且他似乎非常确信自己拿的是A-K。

sentences.en: And oh no, and it was just, and then I had an hour in my room having a panic attack
